title: Influenza A causes placental immune dysregulation without fetal transmission in primates
summary: A study in nonhuman primates found that influenza A infection triggers immune dysregulation in the placenta and fetus without crossing the placental barrier. The virus does not achieve vertical transmission to the developing fetus.
takeaways: Published December 2024 in Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology
Immune dysregulation observed in placental and fetal tissue
No vertical transmission to fetus in primate models
Virus does not cross placental barrier

title: Extracellular matrix–targeted CAR T cells show enhanced persistence against solid tumors
summary: Researchers engineered CAR T cells with a tenascin-C-targeting scFv to enhance persistence and infiltration in solid tumors. This modification improves therapeutic efficacy by enabling better interaction with the tumor extracellular matrix.
takeaways: CAR T cells armored with tenascin-C-targeting scFv (TNC-scFv)
Addresses limited persistence and infiltration in solid tumors
Enhanced recognition and interaction with tumor extracellular matrix
Designed to improve therapeutic efficacy against solid malignancies

The elimination opens species' habitats to logging, mining, oil and gas
